Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "path": "memory/continual_arc_task_54611133.md",
 "content": "# Continual-ARC task 54611133: mark gaps in segmented rectangular outlines

## Reusable rule inferred from demos and verified test
The grid contains a rectangular outline made of a line color, interrupted by gaps; everything else is background. Keep every original cell unchanged, and replace each missing cell that lies *between same-color outline segments on one straight side* with color 2. Do not fill unrelated interior/exterior background. This is a gap-marking task, not a general rectangle fill: output color 2 marks the missing outline cells; original outline cells retain their color.

The outline color and background vary between instances (demos include 4 on 8, 6 on 7, and 5 on 4). Find the rectangular perimeter/side segments and bridge collinear holes only.

## Demo observations (0-based row,column)
- Demo 1, 14x29: color-4 rectangular frame on color-8 background, perimeter around rows 0..12, cols 1..13. A one-cell break on left edge at (3,1) is marked 2. Other outside background remains 8.
- Demo 2, 23x17: color-6 segmented rectangular outline on color-7 background, roughly rows 4..19, cols 4..16. Intervening gaps on straight horizontal/vertical outline runs are marked 2 (including gaps in top/bottom and vertical edges); unrelated background remains 7.
- Demo 3, 18x21: color-5 broken frame on color-4 background, roughly rows 0..10, cols 0..16. Gaps on top/bottom/left perimeter are marked 2; intact frame and background stay unchanged.

## Solved test instance evidence
Task test was 29x12, background 1, outline color 4 at rows 19..25 and columns 2..7. Marked only the gaps between collinear perimeter segments:
- (19,4) = 2: break in top horizontal edge between (19,3) and (19,5).
- (21,2) = 2: break in left vertical edge between rows 20 and 22.
- (25,2),(25,3) = 2: break on lower horizontal edge before existing cells at columns 4..7.
All other cells were kept exactly as input. Submission was confirmed CORRECT with zero wrong attempts.

## Practical method
1. Identify background and the sparse/dominant line color forming a rectangle-like perimeter (can be fragmented).
2. Trace straight horizontal and vertical sides from existing outline segments.
3. For a gap with same-color outline endpoints on the same side, write 2 in the missing intervening cells only.
4. Preserve original pixels and all cells not on a bridged outline gap; verify dimensions before submission.
"
